disagreements.positions: The worry was that agent_2 refreshes at 0.85x of revenue while the others refresh at ~2.4-2.6x. That is not the case. All five refresh at a fraction of k: agent_1 0.85k (k 2.5/2.7 = 2.1-2.3x revenue), agent_2 0.85k (code: amt = MW x 0.85 x k x then-current revenue per MW = 2.04x at k 2.4), agent_3 2.3x flat vs 2.6x growth (0.88k), agent_4 0.83k plus the DC at 15 yrs, agent_5 0.85k. The ~2.4-2.6x figures are new-build k, not refresh.
disagreements.resolution: Refresh at ~0.85 of new-build k is supported by the 10-Q. At 6/30/26, in-service gross PP&E is $40.7B: technology equipment $33.8B and software $0.9B (85%), against data-center equipment and leasehold improvements $6.0B (15%). The reused share is shells, power and cooling. At the fleet k of ~2.6x ($40.7B in-service gross over ~1.5 GW = ~$27M/MW against ~$10.3M/MW of exit-2026 revenue per MW), refresh is ~2.2x of restored revenue. All five sit at 2.0-2.3x, so there is nothing to settle on refresh. The real gap is agent_2's lower new-build k grid (2.1/2.4/2.7 at 25/45/30). The 25% weight on 2.1x is not supported by fleet evidence (only the undisclosed-volume $40M/MW 3-6 month deals point that low), so I restate agent_2 on 2.3/2.6/2.7 at 25/50/25: floored split $12.8 -> $3.8, central -$22.9.
disagreements.evidence: CoreWeave 10-Q Q2-26 PP&E note (fetched); agent_2 model.py (run); 9/17/26 release via Yahoo (the $40M/MW is annualised revenue on ~3-6 month contracts; MW and delivery not disclosed).

disagreements.topic: Discount rate on CoreWeave's own lease obligations (caller note 2)
disagreements.positions: Agent_2 discounts all signed landlord rent at 9.25% (CoreWeave's unsecured credit), which lowered its split DCF ($12.8 -> $9.1 floored; central +$3.3 -> -$4.8). Agents 1, 3, 4 and 5 keep rent inside operating cash flow, at the contract rate during signed customer terms and at WACC after. Agent_1 uses 9% only for stranded rent in its stranding scenario.
disagreements.resolution: Not consistent with the brief or with agent_2's own WACC. The brief splits only customer-contract inflows from creditworthy counterparties and keeps everything else at WACC. More importantly, all five WACCs (11.5-11.6%) sit on a capital structure that excludes the $16.3B operating-lease liability, because adjusted EBITDA is after rent and net debt excludes leases. The equity beta inside that WACC already carries the lease leverage. Pulling rent out at a debt rate while keeping that WACC charges the lease risk twice. One treatment for all five: rent stays inside operating cash flow (agent_2 restated from its own model). As a cross-check, CoreWeave itself discounts its leases at a ~10% weighted average (10-Q), so the alternative would cost ~$8 a share unfloored and ~$1.5 floored on every model. I report that as a sensitivity, not the base.
disagreements.evidence: brief_r4_agent_N.md item 2; 10-Q Q2-26 lease note (weighted-average discount rate 10%, remaining term 12 yrs); agent_2 model.py run in three modes (single / split inflows / split + lease leg).

disagreements.topic: Capacity not tied to named sites (caller note 3)
disagreements.positions: Unnamed MW by agent: agent_1 710 energized (at 10/1) + 647 unattributed (2028) + 180 at named sites with undisclosed MW = 1,537; agent_2 585 energized + 866 contracted (to JV-2, NJ-JV, UK-SCOT, CA-SK, CA-CAL) = 1,451; agent_3 857 energized + ~610 = ~1,467; agent_4 772 energized + 764 contracted = 1,536; agent_5 a 500 MW US-OTHER plug plus allocations = ~1,570 inside a 3.94 GW fleet.
disagreements.resolution: Reconciled arithmetic: contracted power is 4.2 GW at 8/11 plus Niagara 85 MW = ~4,285 MW. Niagara was an LOI then, the company excludes LOIs (they sit in the >1.5 GW), and the definitive lease is from 9/16. Named MW are 990 energized + 1,759 to come = 2,749, so ~1,536 MW is unnamed. Of that, ~772 MW is energized by YE26 (>1.85 GW guide - 990 named - Cheyenne 88). About 0.25 GW more must come online in 2027, because named 2027 deliveries (Dalton P2 153, Helios II 260, PF1 150, Lancaster ~100, Kenilworth ~100-125, Bell SK phase 1) give ~2.75 GW against the >3 GW YE27 guide. The remaining ~0.5 GW lands in 2028 with Indonesia and Helios III. Agent_4 matches the total exactly. Agents 1, 2, 3 and 5 are ~85 MW short because they put Niagara inside 4.2 GW, and agents 2, 3 and 5 also double count it in PIPE-LAND. Agent_5 counts Kenilworth phase 2 and Hammond both inside its plug-filled fleet and as pipeline (~250 expected MW twice). Agent_1 is late on timing (all in 2028). Each effect is under $1 unfloored and ~$0 floored, so the DCF range stands. The allocation is fixed in the review rather than re-run.
disagreements.evidence: sites.md company totals and MW summary; Q2-26 call (LOIs excluded from contracted power; >3 GW active YE27); Blockfusion definitive lease 9/16/26 (via inventory); agent site_coverage rows summed.

disagreements.topic: Floored vs unfloored DCF and the reporting basis (caller note 4)
disagreements.positions: Floored split DCFs as filed: $0 / $9.1 / $4.6 / $1.0 / $8.9. Agents 3 and 5 report gpu_life unfloored, agents 1, 2 and 4 floored. Unfloored figures mix grid means and central cells.
disagreements.resolution: Restated on one basis (Oct-27, rent inside operating cash flow, each agent's own grid, cell-level floor) by running each model: see round4_review.dcf_common_basis. Floored split $0 / $3.8 (agent_2 reconciled) / $4.6 / $1.0 / $8.9, mean $3.7. Unfloored grid means -$39.6 / -$19.2 / -$55.5 / -$37.1 / -$19.2. Central cells -$39.6 / -$22.9 / -$74.2 / -$42.3 / -$27.3. Same reading as round 3: at k ~2.6 the equity's cash-flow value is about zero, and all positive floored value sits in the k <= 2.3, 7-8-yr or shortage cells.
disagreements.evidence: Agents' model scripts run in the supervisor scratch (agent_2 model.py, agent_3 run4.py, agent_4 grid4.py, agent_5 r4.py); agent_1 reported both bases.

disagreements.positions: IG rates: agent_4 7.0%, agents 1 and 2 7.5%, agent_3 8.0%, agent_5 8.1%. Blends 8.06-9.4%. All anchor on DDTL 4.0 (A3, SOFR+225, 2.00% + 3.14-yr UST = ~5.9% at pricing).
disagreements.resolution: The 3-yr UST was 3.81% on 3/31/26 and 4.91% on 10/1/26 (two independent official series agree), so the same loan today costs ~6.9%. With 1.2x DSCR the debt covers ~83% of the contract cash, and the ~17% residual carries completion and operating risk at an equity-like ~13%. That gives ~7.8-8.0% for IG cash (agents 3 and 5 are right; agents 1 and 2 are slightly low but within ~50bp). Agent_4's 7.0% leaves no residual premium and is too low, worth about -$0.5 a share. All five apply the rate only inside signed terms (RPO-based), with post-contract, pipeline and terminal at WACC, as the brief requires.
disagreements.evidence: DDTL 4.0 overview deck (via inventory and agents); US Treasury daily par yields and Fed H.15 (3-yr CMT 3.81% on 3/31/26, 4.91-5.00% on 9/30-10/1/26).

disagreements.positions: agent_1 $92 (6.0x x $19.7B), agent_2 $100, agent_3 $69 (5.2x x $20.3B), agent_4 $81.9 (6.0x x $19.1B NTM, $63.0B net debt incl. JV), agent_5 $97 (6.0x x $20.3B).

Agent_1's site-built 2027 revenue ($24.2B, ~8% below consensus) points the same way. I use ~$19.9B NTM EBITDA at 6.0x, less ~$62.4B net debt including ~$1.4B of JV commitments (flag F5, now in every bridge), over ~625M shares = ~$91. I keep agent_3's 5.2x as the bear mechanism, as in round 3.

Window events are the 35M-share ATM from ~Oct 17, hedging around the $97.85 2033 convert, the Oct 27-28 FOMC and late-October hyperscaler capex commentary. Site coverage and split discounting do not touch the window, and the five 1-month ladders agree within ~1.5pts, so I keep their mean.

Agent_2's lease rate and k grid offset each other, so the reconciled floored DCF ($0-9, mean ~$4) still contributes almost nothing. None of this moves the 12-month price, which follows the ~6x EBITDA multiple and 2027 site delivery. So I keep the forecasters' mean ladder, which moved only ~0.5pt from round 3.

key_drivers: Capex intensity k: fleet ~2.6x ($40.7B in-service gross PP&E over ~1.5 GW = ~$27M/MW against ~$10.3M/MW of revenue). Each 0.1x is ~$11-13 a share unfloored. Refresh is ~0.85k (85% of in-service PP&E is technology and software, 10-Q).
Economic life and re-contract regime: 6->7 yrs is +$30-43, and shortage vs glut is ~$40. Current rents are firm (H100 ~$2.77 on Oct 1), so this is not tested before 2028.

Delivery of ~2.4 GW of contracted-not-energized capacity, ~0.75 GW of it unnamed: >3 GW active at YE27 needs ~0.25 GW of unnamed capacity in 2027, after Helios II slipped a year and Poolside's 250 MW was terminated.

Leverage and rent: ~$62B Oct-27 net debt including JV commitments, plus a $16.3B lease liability (12-yr remaining) that runs whether or not slots are refilled. The split rate adds only ~$3 a share unfloored because signed cash is 0-4 yrs out by Oct-27.

The 12-month price follows ~6x NTM adj. EBITDA (~$19.9B) and AI-capex sentiment. Concentration (Customer A 36% of Q2) and dilution (35M-share ATM, 2033 converts at $97.85) are the near-term overhangs.

Split = signed-contract cash at counterparty rates, everything else at WACC; single = one WACC. Values recomputed by running each agent's own model where it reported only part of this.

sizing.reason: Round 4 confirms round 3. Site-level, split-rate DCFs still put the equity's cash-flow value near zero at the observed ~2.6x capex intensity, so value rests on a ~6x EBITDA multiple and on 2027 delivery. At ~90% vol the stock beats SPY on Sharpe less often than not (0.31). It would add a high-beta leg to an existing AI cluster, with near-term ATM supply and Q3 event risk, so the cap stays at 1.5% (~$150).
